biggest_catch: Chicago election judges are officially paid $170 for Election Day plus $60 for training — but the official handbook says payment arrives by mail within 4 to 6 weeks, failing the lane's speed rule.
catches: Official payment arrives by mail 4–6 weeks after Election Day — not same-day or days.
It is a ~15.5-hour day (5AM to roughly 8:30PM, sometimes later) for the $170 Election Day portion.
Training pay ($60) is only received if you also serve on Election Day.
Pay can be prorated for substitute, late, or early-departing judges.

c1.evidence: Official Chicago Board of Elections materials describe the election judge program, duties, and application.

c2.evidence: Official High School Judge FAQ: '$170 for serving on Election Day and $60 for completing an inperson training.' Official 2023 handbook: '$170 for successfully serving all day on Election Day' plus 'an additional $60 payment' after training.

c3.evidence: Official election judge handbook: 'You should receive payment by mail within 4 to 6 weeks after Election Day.' Weeks, not days.

c4.evidence: No fee; it is paid civic service.

eligibility: Registered Cook County voters (plus eligible high school/college student judges); must complete training and serve the full day
maximize: Not a same-day route — official timing is 4–6 weeks by mail. As civic side income it is real, but do not count on it for fast cash; apply at pollworker.chicagoelections.gov well before the election.
notes: A qualifying civic-pay program with fully official pay terms, but the 4–6-week mailed payment fails this lane's today-or-days rule. Honest reject for the lane; legitimate civic income otherwise.
payout_quote: $170 for serving on Election Day and $60 for completing an inperson training (official Board FAQ).
